characters.name: Frankie Heck
characters.description: The overstressed matriarch of the Heck family, and the series' narrator. Big Eater: ARunning Gagis her eating a lot. She kept her maternity pants to use on Thanksgiving. Butt-Monkey: Very often, though not as much as her daughter, Sue. You could argue that it's an entire family ofButt Monkeys, but those two stand out the most. Catchphrase:When Mike says something to Sue with his usualBrutal Honesty, Frankie will usually tell Sue, "I think what your dadmeansto say is-" before saying something that's more gentle or supportive."You do for family." When Mike says something to Sue with his usualBrutal Honesty, Frankie will usually tell Sue, "I think what your dadmeansto say is-" before saying something that's more gentle or supportive.

characters.name: Mike Heck
characters.description: Frankie's stoic but well-meaning husband who manages the Orson Limestone quarry. Agent Scully: Absolutely won't entertain the notion that Sue saw a vision of the Santa Maria in "Halloween IV" Big Brother Bully: He was this to his brother in their youth. Brutal Honesty: He is known for his straightforward manner. Characterization Marches On: Mike had more of a typical "bumbling TV dad" personality in the first couple of episodes. He would soon go on to become theOnly Sane Manof the family.

characters.name: Axl Heck
characters.description: Frankie and Mike's oldest son, your typical rebellious and moody teenager who's at an age when he wants nothing to do with his parents. The Ace: He's handsome, funny, and charming when he wants to be. Best Her to Bed Her: Tries this on his love interest in Season 6, with a variety of sports:she lets him win at pool. Big Brother Bully: He's horrible to Sue most of the time. Big Brother Instinct: While Axl shows more affection towards his little brother, Brick, he's more emotionally closed off when it comes to his little sister, Sue. He treats her with disdain, taunts and teases her to no end, and belittles her very existence (he never tells anyone in his school that he has a sister)... but when it comes down to it, Axl shows a softer, comforting side of him when it really counts.

characters.name: Sue Heck
characters.description: Frankie and Mike's quirky and often high-strung but optimistic and determined middle daughter. Annoying Younger Sibling: At least, Axl feels like this about her. Beware the Nice Ones: It's rare, but if you actually succeed in making Sue angry, you better watch out. Axl has learned this the hard way on multiple occasions. Big Sister Instinct: She can be this to Brick, to both positive and negative effect. But either way, it is clear that she loves her little brother. Born Unlucky: She's the most unpopular person in school, she failed her driving test six times, a deer ran into her and broke her leg and overall, the entire world conspires against her. None of this, though deters her sage-like Pollyanna attitude, and she usually gets a good hand out of it all.

characters.name: Brick Heck
characters.description: Frankie and Mike's highly intelligent but severely socially challenged youngest son. Adorably Precocious Child: In early seasons. Despite his young age he is very smart and well-read. Bad Liar: He has a pretty obvious tell:Brick: (whispering) I'm lying! Big Eater: A lesser extent compared to Axl, but Brick has his moments.In "The Map", he and Axl try and create a model Indiana cake out of brownie mix, pancake mix, and pizzas. The brothers end up devouring all of them. As for the pizza model they ordered two so they could eat one and use the other for the model; they end up eating both of them.Once again demonstrated in the Season Four Halloween episode, he ate 20 pounds of candy in 24 hours. As a result, he started behaving more "normal" for a day until he fainted during dinner. While his parents were glad to have the "old Brick" back, they agreed to giving him a little sugar for "special occasions".Mike: He's more sugar than boy. ... Nobody EVER needs to know about this.In "Thanksgiving VIII", he ate five pounds of bacon bits [as a shift meal] while working at Spudsy's, shocking both his boss and his sister.Brick: My mom ate my breakfast. In "The Map", he and Axl try and create a model Indiana cake out of brownie mix, pancake mix, and pizzas. The brothers end up devouring all of them. As for the pizza model they ordered two so they could eat one and use the other for the model; they end up eating both of them.

characters.name: "Big Mike" Heck
characters.description: Mike's reclusive, seldom-spoken widower father. Cannot Spit It Out: He will not talk about his feelings under any circumstances. The closest he gets to a tender moment in the show is bluntly pointing out that the last time he and his sons were together on thanksgiving, their mother was alive. Collector of the Strange: He is a hoarder of appliances. Grumpy Old Man: He's a recluse who is uncomfortable with emotional displays. I Call It "Vera": Mike says he used to call his belt 'The Enforcer'.

characters.name: Rusty Heck
characters.description: Mike's irresponsible, unreliable, and dimwitted but well-intentioned brother. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: He has a habit of saying and doing random things without thinking it through. Some of his more notable moments include planning a wedding at Mike and Frankie's house without telling either of them about it, stealing a cop's furniture out of their house, and believing that he and Mike share a telepathic bond. Collector of the Strange: He had dozens of jars of "pet dirt" as a kid. Only Known by Their Nickname: Mike heard his real name Orville in court once. He thought it was weird.

characters.name: Tag Spence
characters.description: Frankie's schmoozer father. Abhorrent Admirer: Non-romantic example. Whenever the Spences visit the Hecks, he follows Mike around like a puppy. It probably has something to do with the fact that he never had a son of his own. Dad the Veteran: He was a file clerk in the Korean war. Dangerous Senior Driver: In "Flirting with Disaster", it's shown he's become dangerously bad at driving since his vision has gotten worse in his old age. Granola Guy: Goes through a phase of this. He calls crackers poison and claims that refined sugar has killed more people than Al Qaeda.

characters.name: Pat Spence
characters.description: Frankie's doting mother.

characters.name: Ginny Freehold
characters.description: One of Frankie's aunts. Character Death: She dies at the age of 100. The family attend her funeral in "The Map" Hidden Depths: She met General Patton in her (relative) youth. Informed Attribute: Apparently, she loved a good party. Passed in Their Sleep: Which causes Brick a good deal of anxiety. After all, he sleeps every day!

characters.name: Edie Freehold
characters.description: Another of Frankie's aunts. The Alcoholic: Was known for always having hard liquor on hand and tries to send her nieces and nephews to buy her more. Character Death: Dies at the age of 96, the family attend her funeral in "Hecks on a Train". Cool Old Lady: Axl and Sue come to this conclusion after talking to her for a while and hearing her cool stories Never Mess with Granny: In "The Math Class" she sprays a guy with a garden hose.

characters.name: Dutch Spence
characters.description: Tag's older brother and Frankie's paternal uncle. Always Someone Better: To his younger brother, Tag.

characters.name: Bob Weaver
characters.description: Frankie's closest coworker at Ehlert Motors. Abhorrent Admirer: He's a non-romantic example towards Mike. Bob really likes Mike and wants to be best friends with him, but Mike doesn't like Bob because he's annoying and needy. Basement Dweller: It's been mentioned he lives with his mom. However, in "A Christmas Gift", he says he had to move out becauseshe kicked him out of her house for spilling juice on her couch. Butt-Monkey: He hasMr. Ehlertfor a boss, he has no friends except Frankie, he has bad luck with women, his own relatives don't like him, and he generally just has a lot of bad luck. Can't Take Criticism: In "The Yelling", he has a panic attack and runs around screaming just because Mike told him he's a little needy, sometimes.

characters.name: Don Ehlert
characters.description: Frankie's first boss and the owner and founder of Orson's only surviving car dealership, Ehlert Motors. Bad Boss: Treats his employees with no respect and makes them work on holidays Corrupt Corporate Executive: Engages in several shady or downright illegal business practices, like tricking Frankie into taking him to a colonoscopy and falsely advertising his cars. Hate Sink: Don Ehlert is the owner of Ehlert Motors and a greedy and very unscrupulous businessman. He constantly exhibited sexist and racist behaviors, constantly made Francis "Frankie" Heck's life difficult when she worked for him and encouraged employees to sell to people who were drunk because they'd be easy to take advantage of. By the time Ehlert made his final appearance in the series, his business seemed to be failing and no one cared about or appreciated his attempts to try to force interest in advertising it anymore. It's All About Me: Frankie describes him as "the most selfish man in the world"

characters.name: Brad Bottig
characters.description: Sue's first real "boyfriend", whose homosexuality she seems to be unaware of. Alliterative Name:BradBottig. Camp Gay: He's a flamboyant theatre kid who tends to wear colorful, bold clothing. Nice Guy: Brad is a cheerful, energetic young man who is hard to upset. He often tries to resolve disputes through dance fights. Perpetual Smiler: Being asked not to smile when he wants to smile seems to cause him physical pain.

characters.name: Carly
characters.description: Sue's initial best friend. She Cleans Up Nicely: In seasons 1 and 3. Her braces were removed mid-Season 1, and she became more popular as a result.

characters.name: Nancy Donahue
characters.description: The matriarch of an idealistic family that lives in the same neighborhood as the Hecks do. Abusive Parents:Became very hard on Sean after he became aGranola Guy Always Someone Better: Somehow spending a week with her caused an elderly dogto regrow lung tissue. Not So Above It All: She's usually hard to upset, but she pushes Frankie into a pool on vacation after learning that she gossiped to Mike about Nancy being an overbearing parent. Parental Substitute: Seems to do a lot of things with the Heck children that Mike and Frankie don't wanna do. Apparently she taught Sue how to ride a bike.She also taught Axl how to brush his teeth.

characters.name: Sean Donahue
characters.description: One of Axl's best friends, and Nancy's oldest son. Academic Athlete: Sean is the smartest of him, Axl and Darrin. He gets good grades and was even accepted to Notre Dame. Deadpan Snarker: Has shades of this. Dogged Nice Guy: Sort of. Sean has no romantic interest in Sueat firstbut he has twice, out of the kindness of his own heart, driven all the way down from Notre Dame (blowing off his own studies in the process) to be Sue's date only to be rejected because Sue found someone else at the last minute. Granola Guy: Became this in season 7, his mother was not impressed. Reverted to normal in season 8 after a pep talk from Frankie encouraging him to pursue medicine again.

characters.name: DarrinMcGrew
characters.description: Another of Axl's best friends. Brainless Beauty: How his ex-girlfriend Angel saw him. The Ditz: Not the brightest boy. Dumb Jock: He's also a teammate on Axl's football team. The Friend Nobody Likes: Axl began treating him like this whenhe started dating Sue

characters.name: Reverend "Tim-Tom" Thomas
characters.description: A popular youth pastor whom Sue finds to be the first person that truly "gets" her. Birds of a Feather: With "Reverend Tammy" Full-Name Basis: He always addresses Sue as "Sue Heck", to show that he will always remember her name, as he seems aware that hardly anyone else does. Intergenerational Friendship: With Sue Mentor Archetype: Sue always looks to him for advice and he always seems to appear just as Sue needs help the most. Also once gave advice to Axl.

characters.name: The Glossners
characters.description: A poor, chaotic, badly-disciplined family that lives across the street from the Hecks. The Alcoholic: Rita is always seen holding a beer bottle. Diaper Glossner acts like this despite being way too young to drink. All Girls Want Bad Boys: WhySueis so attracted to Derrick Glossner. Ax-Crazy: Often seen picking fights, threatening neighbors, and causing property damage. Rita also has at least two'strikes', implying that she's been convicted of at least two violent crimes. Betty and Veronica: With respect to Sue, Derrick was the Veronica to Daren's Betty.

characters.name: Zack
characters.description: A friend of Brick's from his social skills class. Cloud Cuckoolander: Thinks he's a cat and frequently meows, nearly always wears mittens on his hands to keep himself from scratching things.By the time of the final season, he and the others in Brick's social group have outgrown their quirks.

characters.name: Morgan Edwards
characters.description: One of Axl's girlfriends.

characters.name: Matt
characters.description: One of Sue's boyfriends and a competitive wrestler. Official Couple: With Sue in seasons 2 and 3. Put on a Bus: He transferred to another school and left Sue for a girl named Kerry.

characters.name: "Weird Ashley" Wyman
characters.description: A classmate of Axl's with an unrequited interest in him. She has a fondness for all things related to wicca. Abhorrent Admirer: To Axl. Cloudcuckoolander: Hence the nickname. She believes in magic and has a reputation for trying to cast spells on people. Hollywood Voodoo: Seems to practice this. Ironically, she's never heard ofHarry Potteruntil Frankie and Mike allude to it. Running Gag: Somehow, Axl always ends up going to prom with her. Even Sue went with her once.

characters.name: Courtney and Debbie
characters.description: Two pretty but shallow cheerleaders and acquaintances of Axl and Sue. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Can never remember Sue exists no matter how often they meet. In one episode, they made fun of Sue's idea of having a watch party forIts The Great Pumpkin Charlie Brownin a pumpkin patch, then held a watch party in a graveyard for a horror movie on the same night. Depending on the Writer: Whether their malicious actions, especially towards Sue, are the result of ill will or sheer stupidity varies depending on the episode. Cloudcuckoolanders: Sue greets them while they're waiting on Axl at the Hecks'. Not only do they not remember having ever spoken to her but — because they don't believe Axl has a sister — they tell him that "there's this poor girl who's lost in your house." The Dividual: Axl has a problem when he realizes that he doesn't knowwhich one he's actually dating.

characters.name: Dr. Fulton
characters.description: The guidance counselor at Orson Elementary. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: When Brick asked why it was important that he make friends his own age, he told him he didn't know, but begged Brick to do it since his job was on the line. Crazy Cat Lady: Male example. He lives in a small apartment with lots of cats. No Social Skills: For a guidance counselor, he talks about his own problems a lot during sessions.

characters.name: Principal Larimer
characters.description: Stern Teacher: Is intimidating towards the parents in parent-teacher conferences as well.

characters.name: Principal Barker
characters.description: Get Out!: To Mike and Frankie

characters.name: Ms. Rinsky
characters.description: Casting Gag: Her dynamic with Frankie is an obvious nod to that of Debra and Marie's inEverybody Loves Raymond, with Ms. Rinsky patronizing and criticizing Frankie like Marie did to Debra. However, one difference between the two relationships is that Ms. Rinsky is the one who considers Frankie to be a "smother", and believes that no child benefits from helicopter parenting. The Comically Serious: Her surly attitude can be pretty humorous. Cool Teacher: Zig-Zagged. Most of the time, she's cranky and sarcastic,but other people like Brick and a school faculty member describe her as "wonderful"and she gives her students candy for every question they answer right. She also likes Brick to a certain degree, outright stating to Frankie that he makes her laugh. Jerkass Has a Point: Aside from the way she treats Frankie, giving Brick a D- on his math test for only answering three questions just so he could have free reading time is fair. Jerkass to One: She's very condescending and unpleasant to Frankie.

characters.name: Arlo
characters.description: Another student in Brick's social skills class. Cloud Cuckoolander: As one of Brick's fellow socially-challenged friends, he has an obsession with keeping everything on a schedule and takes frequent and lengthy bathroom breaks. [[folder:Dr. Ted Goodwin]] A dentist who becomes Frankie's second boss when she takes up work as his hygienist. Benevolent Boss: Is very friendly and sociable with Frankie.

characters.name: Edwin
characters.description: The owner of Spudsy's, a baked potato restaurant where Sue works in high school and college. Hidden Depths: While he's the manager at Spudsy's, Sue and Brick both agree that he is a very good actor, and he's auditioning for a role onSNL.

characters.name: Cassidy Finch
characters.description: One of Axl's girlfriends. Betty and Veronica: Chose Axl (Veronica) over a smarter, older boy. Big Damn Kiss: With Axl after he won a football match. Crush Blush: Does this when she leaves the room after Axl'sForceful Kiss. Love Makes You Crazy: Why she forgave Axl for starting a fire in her backyard.

characters.name: Kenny
characters.description: Axl and Hutch's mysterious, silent college roommate who seemingly does nothing but play video games, though there's more than meets the eye. The Faceless: For many of his appearances, he is shown exclusively from the back or with his face behind a computer screen. The Ghost: Sort of. He can always be seen, but hardly ever speaks, and he seemingly doesn't do anything except sit with his back to the camera playing video games. Hidden Depths: In season 7, he reveals to Frankie that his family situation isn't typical. He's also skilled in IT, helping Frankie with her computer and wi-fi, and is extremely talented at making grilled cheese sandwiches.In the season 8 finale, it's revealed that he's been developing apps in between games the whole time, perhaps using games as a front to protect his ideas from being stolen by shoulder-peepers, and has a high enough net worth from them that he will be able to retire within one year after leaving college. In the season 8 finale, it's revealed that he's been developing apps in between games the whole time, perhaps using games as a front to protect his ideas from being stolen by shoulder-peepers, and has a high enough net worth from them that he will be able to retire within one year after leaving college.

characters.name: Hutch Hutchinson
characters.description: Axl's best college friend and roommate. Black Best Friend: To Axl. Butt-Monkey: He and Axl met getting bullied by the Older Football players. Character Development:In season 9, after graduating college and moving into his own Chicago apartment, he starts acting more like a responsible adult, inspiring Axl to do the same. Heterosexual Life-Partners: Again with Axl especially since they decided to live together.

characters.name: Devin Levin
characters.description: Axl's first college girlfriend. Birds of a Feather: With Axl. Distaff Counterpart: Of Axl. The Lad-ette: She's an athletic tomboy who dislikes many typically feminine things and activities. Official Couple: With Axluntil Season 7.

characters.name: Cindy Hornberger
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: Somewhat, as evidenced by her kicking Mike's car and Brick's nervous, "No, she won't," when Mike says she'll get over him not saving her seat on the bus. Bizarre Taste in Food: When Frankie asked if she wanted something to eat she requested shrimp; for her Thanksgiving meal she had a hunk of cheese. In both cases, she took a single bite then stopped. Cleans Up Nicely: When she gets dressed up for the prom in "Great Heckspectations," she's sostunninglygorgeousthat Frankie worries another guy will steal her from Brick.She needn't have worried; Brick and Cindy skip the prom and sneak into the library, having mutually agreed it was a much better use of their time. Cloudcuckoolander: Gives Brick a run for his money. Creepy Monotone: At all times.

characters.name: Troy
characters.description: A friend Brick makes in middle school. Gentle Giant: He comes from a big family where apparently he's the smallest one so he protects Brick from being picked on. Power Trio: With Brick and Cindy. Shrinking Violet: Is quite shy and admits he doesn't make friends very easily.

characters.name: Lexie Brooks
characters.description: Sue's well-to-do college rival, and later her best friend. Always Someone Better: How Sue originally saw her. Deadpan Snarker: Axl or sleep-deprivation can bring this out in her. Genki Girl: Why she and Sue became friends. Official Couple: Her and Axl (Lexl) as of Season 8.

characters.name: Logan
characters.description: A handsome young man whom Sue crushes on. Mr. Fanservice: Has a job that requires him not to wear a shirt; this is heavilyLampshaded. Sexy Priest: Studying to be one.

characters.name: Holly Haypek
characters.description: Alliterative Name:HollyHaypek Really Gets Around: Is said to bring numerous boys to the room and kick Sue out so she can sleep with them. Straw Nihilist: Puts up a poster saying *** Life, claims she doesn't like people.

characters.name: Jeremy
characters.description: Sue's temporary college boyfriend and an over-the-top left-wing activist. Derailing Love Interests: It really doesn't take long for Sue to get tired of him and his far left-wing diatribes. Establishing Character Moment: Chained to a tree yelling at Sue through a megaphone. Foil: To Mike, in a way. During Jeremy's first dinner with the Hecks, the two clash on various subjects in a manner reminiscent of adifferent Mike arguing with a far left-wing love interest of his daughter. Granola Guy: Environmentalist, socialist, vegan, and more. He briefly shaves his hippie beard to flirt with Sue before growing it back in full a few appearances later.
